newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 25.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

In his last major interview before the budget Chancellor Kenneth Clarke warned the electorate not to expect a "Santa Claus budget". He discussed the housing market, which he said was improving strongly and looked forward to the General Election where he urged Conservative candidates not to defy the party line and come out against a single European currency.
IMRO SET TO GIVE ALL-CLEAR AT JUPITER

Following a seven months investigation of management practices at Jupiter Tyndall, the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation is expected to announce its findings. It is anticipated that allegations of wrongdoing against the fund manager will be dismissed.
A NEW FUND FRONTIER IN EASTERN EUROPE

A new Eastern Europe fund venture has been set up by a group of British and Russian investment fund managers, who are combining hedge fund techniques with a more conventional stock-picking approach. The Muscovy Frontiers Fund with a value of $100 million (62.5 million stg) is aimed at equities in the former eastern bloc and is being marketed to City institutions.
RISKS REMAIN DESPITE RUSSIA'S BIG REVIVAL

The floodgates have opened to Russian companies looking for exposure on Western markets, following the success of this week's 240 million stg shares offering in Gazprom, the Russian gas corporation. Merchant International Group recently rated Russia as the most risky emerging market in the world. Foreign enthusiasm for investment in Russia can be explained by the fact the Moscow Times 50-share index soared by 50 percent in the first six months of this year.
